How to Build a Cozy Fireplace Fire (That Won't Get Smoky) | The Art of Manliness

Everything about this is wrong.

For starters, you aren't going to hold a burning piece of paper "for a couple minutes."

Second, you do not put your kindling on top for a fireplace fire. I know, the idea is to create embers which fall down and burn the next sized kindling, and so on. Unfortunately, they tell you "log, then smaller log, then paper." Paper on that level of quantity is not going to light a branch sized piece of wood on fire. You would need leaves, twigs, small branches, and so on.

Third, if you really want to call this "prepping," learn how to make a fire without paper.

You can hold a paper for a while if it is rolled tight enough to reduce oxygen.

I have made fireplace fires using the method listed here. The key is a good middle stage which bridges the quick burning kindling into the larger logs.

Not really prepping, but interesting enough. More like an "Every man should know" type thing.

Side personal note. Makes me remember Christmas at grandma's. We always made a fire there around this time of year. Wasn't really for heat, but it creates a great atmosphere.

Yeah, open fireplaces are pretty but suck in cold air. Just bought a 1940 house where the fireplace was not only never used but it’s capped and the chimney was never lined. So I put some wood and red Christmas lights in there, crumpled some celophane, hid a small fan in it. Out of the corner of your eye, you’d swear there’s a real fire in there. I have family visiting and when they first got here, they’d keep moving closer to get warm before they realized what they were doing.

Rolling up paper can work but only if you’re not fighting weather. Plus, in a survival situation, you’re not likely to have spare paper to burn.

Note that fireplaces are horrible at heating efficiency. Most fireplaces in new homes are just for decoration. As TFA says you'll have to crack a window open; it'll make it "cozy" by heating things close to the fireplace but things further away will wind up colder. Wood stoves are much more efficient at heating than fireplaces.

If you want to have a cozy fireplace and have it be practical, do it more than a couple of times per winter, you're going to need to buy a "stove insert". This is basically a wood stove designed to be installed inside a fireplace and give the best of both worlds. They're not cheap and can be tricky to emplace though.
